reason: B offers the cleaner, more physically plausible mechanism: Co tends to stabilize low-fault-energy states, so its removal can raise effective stacking-fault energy and suppress twinning, testable by matched interrupted tests and twin-density measurements. A relies on the unsupported premise that removing Co necessarily increases lattice distortion and lowers stacking-fault energy, while ambiguously combining twinning and dynamic strain aging in a non-decisive falsification rule.
